summary:
A trans visitor to South Carolina enters under the United States federal document and screening regime before state law applies. Executive Order 14168, signed 20 January 2025, requires federal identity documents to reflect sex assigned at birth; the State Department has stopped processing the X marker and any marker not matching sex assigned at birth, issuing new passports only as M or F, while previously issued X-marker passports remain valid until expiry. The Supreme Court allowed those restrictions to take effect in November 2025, and trans and nonbinary travellers report passports confiscated or blocked at processing, with some left stranded abroad.

Entry screening adds exposure. The State Department announced on 25 February 2025 that it would bar trans athletes from entering the United States to compete in women's sports, flags visa applicants with an internal marking, and treats a declared gender other than the one assigned at birth as fraud carrying a permanent bar. Transportation Security Administration checkpoint procedures can involve secondary screening, hand-held devices and pat-downs that risk outing a trans traveller.

Facilities are the sharpest South Carolina-specific exposure. Governor Henry McMaster signed House Bill 4756 into law on 15 May 2026, requiring transgender students in South Carolina public schools, colleges and universities to use restrooms matching their sex assigned at birth. The Senate amended the bill before passage, and the ACLU of South Carolina issued a response on 18 May 2026 framing it as discrimination against trans students in both K-12 and higher education.

The measure extends a pre-existing restriction on school restrooms into campus settings. A July 2026 anti-trans national legal risk assessment, which ranks states on the severity of adult and youth law by reading bills, places South Carolina among the escalating states rather than in the harshest tier.

Custody carries a further state-layer restriction: South Carolina operates a "freeze-frame" policy limiting the treatments transgender inmates may receive while incarcerated. Federal custody is separately affected by the Bureau of Prisons adoption of Florida-based policies for transgender inmates from 2026, which mandate short haircuts, withdrawal of hormone medication and substitution of psychiatric therapy and psychiatric drugs, and by the Bureau's cessation of reporting the number of transgender prisoners it holds from 2025.
tangentialFactors:
South Carolina sits within a wider facilities pattern. Bathroom bans applying to trans people in K-12 schools and, in some states, government buildings cover 9 states and 1 territory, and some states make trans use of facilities a criminal offence in certain circumstances, while 29 states, 4 territories and the District of Columbia have no such ban. In April 2025 a trans student was arrested and handcuffed in a women's restroom at the Florida state capitol after declaring an intention to break the law, an arrest civil-rights attorneys described as the first known under a state bathroom-restriction law.

South Carolina's freeze-frame treatment policy is shared with three other states, Tennessee, Arkansas and Utah, according to the Transitics tracker cited by Metro Weekly on 11 July 2026, which places the state within a small group rather than at the extreme of custodial practice.

Document and care measures at other state level show the direction of travel. In March 2026 Kansas enacted a law invalidating birth certificates and driver's licences that do not match sex assigned at birth and barring trans people from sex-segregated facilities, which rights groups call a template for other state legislatures. Gender-affirming care for children is banned in 27 states, and Executive Order 14187 of 28 January 2025 described such care for minors as mutilation, with the Department of Justice subpoenaing more than 20 hospitals in summer 2025 for full records of patients under 19.

Several federal measures in force or in litigation, including the military purge under Executive Order 14183, the women's sports ban under Executive Order 14201, a January 2025 federal funding freeze and an October 2025 rule blocking student loan forgiveness for public workers who provide gender-affirming care to transgender youth, have been blocked or enjoined in court, so the operative position on any given measure should be checked before travel.
localsOnly:
South Carolina's freeze-frame policy restricts the treatments transgender inmates may receive while incarcerated. It is one of four states with Tennessee, Arkansas and Utah holding such policies, per the Transitics tracker cited by Metro Weekly on 11 July 2026. The restriction concerns in-prison treatment rather than housing placement.

No South Carolina case or ruling on cell placement, special units, or solitary or segregation for trans prisoners is recorded in the sources underpinning this assessment.

House Bill 4756 binds transgender students resident in the state across public schools, colleges and universities, so the restroom provision shapes daily life for students rather than only visitors. The ACLU of South Carolina, which responded to the governor's signature on 18 May 2026, is the named state-level civil-rights body contesting the measure.

Conditions for changing a gender marker on a South Carolina licence or birth certificate differ from state to state across the United States, and equality-map research shows no uniform national procedure; a resident's options turn on South Carolina's own process, which is not set out in the sources assembled here.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources assembled here contain no South Carolina provision on birth certificates or driver's licences, so the state's rules for changing a gender marker remain unresolved rather than confirmed as open or closed.

Enforcement detail for House Bill 4756, including who verifies restroom use, the penalties attached, and any litigation filed against it, is not sourced here.

Whether South Carolina falls among the 27 states banning gender-affirming care for children, or has adopted a Medicaid reimbursement restriction, is not established in this inventory.

The status of legal challenges to the federal passport restrictions remains contested: the Human Rights Campaign records that the policy is still challenged in federal courts, and the ACLU's suit on behalf of seven plaintiffs is unresolved in the material available, so the operative federal position should be rechecked before travel.

No recorded South Carolina case or ruling on cell placement, special units, or solitary or segregation for trans prisoners appears in these sources, leaving the state's placement framework unresolved.
